name: GitHub
approval: No standard provider review for OAuth app registration
summary: Create a GitHub OAuth app in minutes, but first choose between an OAuth app and a GitHub App. GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for modern integrations because permissions are more granular.
decision: If you need access to individual repositories or agent actions, evaluate a GitHub App first. Use a classic OAuth app only if its user-level authorization model fits.

branches.name: Classic OAuth app
branches.detail: Registration is self-service. No published manual approval stage for ordinary OAuth app registration.

branches.name: GitHub App (often preferred)
branches.detail: Fine-grained permissions and installability; separate app registration and token handling.

requirements.title: GitHub account with app registration rights
requirements.detail: Personal account or an organization where you have administrative access.

requirements.title: Public app homepage + callback URL
requirements.detail: Provide a homepage and correct authorization callback; GitHub currently supports multiple callback URLs.

requirements.title: Secure server-side code exchange
requirements.detail: Keep client secret off the browser, validate state, handle token expiry/revocation.

steps.title: Choose OAuth app or GitHub App
steps.detail: Map required actions to permission model. Consider GitHub App installation and fine-grained repository permissions first.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.detail: Settings → Developer settings → OAuth apps → New OAuth App. Enter public name, homepage and authorization callback URL.

steps.title: Implement and test authorization
steps.detail: Agent can generate state validation, callback handler and token exchange; you supply client credentials using environment secrets and authorize a test account.

steps.title: Test another user and go live
steps.detail: Confirm consent screen, scopes, refresh/expiration behavior, error handling, and unlink flows. No generic provider approval submission documented for classic app registration.

blockers.solution: Use a GitHub App when you need repository-scoped installations, organization approval or independent app actions.
Register the exact callback URL and ensure the redirect URI used in your authorization flow is an allowed one.
Ask the organization owner to approve the application; this is workspace-specific, not general GitHub marketplace approval.

agentCan: Compare requested actions with GitHub permission models
Generate OAuth callback, state, token-storage code
Write a test matrix and checklist
humanMust: Own the GitHub account and register the app
Securely configure credentials and authorize accounts

name: Slack
approval: Unlisted: no Marketplace review; Marketplace: up to 10 business days preliminary + up to 10 weeks functional
summary: A Slack app can reach early pilot users through unlisted distribution, but commercial distribution at scale points toward Slack Marketplace approval, with workspace installs and review queues as key blockers.
decision: Launch a controlled pilot through unlisted distribution, then pursue Marketplace listing once you have 10 active workspace installations and production-ready onboarding.

branches.name: Unlisted distribution / pilot
branches.time: Hours of setup; customer admin approval may vary
branches.detail: Activate distribution after HTTPS and OAuth setup. Appropriate for early pilots, not a substitute for Marketplace for commercial scale.

branches.name: Slack Marketplace listing
branches.time: Up to 10 business days + 10 weeks review (published ceilings)
branches.detail: Requires at least 10 installations on active workspaces throughout review and functional/security checks.

requirements.title: Slack developer app + OAuth scopes
requirements.detail: Configure bot/user scopes appropriate to functionality; avoid unsupported/restricted scopes for Marketplace.

requirements.title: Public HTTPS callback and endpoints
requirements.detail: SSL is required for OAuth redirects and interactive/event request URLs used for distribution.

requirements.title: Ten active workspaces for Marketplace submission
requirements.detail: As of July 2026, maintain 10+ installs on active workspaces throughout review; active means used in prior 28 days.

requirements.title: Install/uninstall tests, listing and reviewer access
requirements.detail: Test from a workspace other than development, provide production-ready documentation and credentials for reviewers when needed.

steps.title: Create app and choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Start at Slack API app dashboard. Define granular scopes and redirect URL; decide pilot vs Marketplace upfront.

steps.title: Implement OAuth installation flow
steps.detail: Agent writes authorize/callback, token exchange, state checking and workspace token storage. Human configures HTTPS domain and client secret.

steps.title: Activate unlisted distribution
steps.detail: In app dashboard → Manage Distribution, complete checklist and activate public distribution for pilot users.

steps.title: Qualify for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Acquire/maintain 10 active installed workspaces, test installation and uninstall in a separate workspace, prepare support/docs and reviewer accounts.

steps.title: Submit, address feedback and publish
steps.detail: Submit from Slack app settings; preliminary review can take up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks for new listings.

blockers.solution: Check that at least 10 workspaces with installations are active; requirement persists during review.
Have the target workspace admin approve the app or request installation through the workspace flow.

blockers.problem: Review comes back with scope issues
blockers.solution: Reduce scopes to functionality actually implemented, provide a demo and updated reviewer instructions.

Check the scope list against planned features
Prepare reviewer test plan and compliance checklist
humanMust: Sign in, create and distribute the Slack app
Securely provision production HTTPS endpoints and secrets
Recruit pilot workspaces and respond to reviewer feedback

Workspace-specific admin restrictions are not predictable before installation.

name: Google APIs
approval: Simple scopes: path depends on brand requirements; sensitive: typically 3–5 business days; restricted: potentially weeks + assessment
summary: Scope selection determines launch risk. Low-risk sign-in is different from Calendar, Drive, or restricted Gmail access. A restricted-scope app accessing data through servers may need an independent security assessment.
decision: Identify the exact API methods and minimum scopes before building. Do not commit to a Google launch date until sensitive/restricted scope classification and verification exceptions are known.

branches.name: Sign-in / non-sensitive scopes
branches.time: Hours of engineering; branding process may apply
branches.detail: Review relevant branding and publication requirements; non-sensitive is not a blanket guarantee of zero verification.

branches.name: Sensitive scopes
branches.detail: Requires accurate consent-screen details, verified domains, rationale and feature video; may require additional iteration.

branches.name: Restricted scopes
branches.detail: If restricted Google data passes through/gets stored on servers, annual third-party security assessment can apply.

requirements.title: Cloud project, enabled APIs, OAuth consent branding
requirements.detail: Set up Branding, Audience and Data Access, provide app name, contacts and policy URLs where required.

requirements.title: Domain ownership and valid redirect URLs
requirements.detail: For verification, verify domain ownership and use compliant authorized domains / HTTPS production redirect URIs.

requirements.title: Minimal scope inventory
requirements.detail: Classify each scope as non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted; determine whether an exception applies.

requirements.title: Evidence packet for review
requirements.detail: For sensitive/restricted scopes, prepare feature demo, scope justification, functional privacy policy and contact details.

steps.title: List operations and choose least-privileged scopes
steps.detail: Map every agent action to Google API methods and required scopes, flag sensitive or restricted labels in Cloud Console.

steps.title: Create project, app branding and OAuth client
steps.detail: Human signs into Google Cloud, enables APIs, configures OAuth Audience/Branding/Data Access and redirect URIs, and stores the client credentials securely.

steps.title: Build and test end-user connection
steps.detail: Agent can create consent URL, callback, CSRF state handling, refresh-token storage and failure-case test scripts; human authorizes test accounts.

steps.title: Prepare scope-specific verification packet
steps.detail: Verify owned domains, homepage and privacy policy; record demo video showing requested permissions and feature use.

steps.title: Submit review and resolve follow-up
steps.detail: Track status in Google Cloud Verification Center and respond to Trust & Safety; restricted-scope security assessment can add weeks.
steps.time: Days to weeks depending on scopes

blockers.solution: Inspect requested scopes and Publishing / Verification status; confirm test-user exception vs production obligations.
Use domains you control, verify in Search Console, align homepage, redirect URI, Terms and privacy policy.

blockers.problem: Restricted scope triggers costly security assessment
blockers.solution: Redesign to narrower scope or avoid sending restricted data through servers when technically possible; confirm applicability with Google.

agentCan: Audit API actions and find least-privilege scopes
Draft consent screen text, privacy policy checklist and demonstration script
Generate OAuth code and review packet
humanMust: Own and verify the required domain
Create Cloud project, authorize consent and protect credentials
Submit verification and commission any required security assessment

name: Notion
approval: Public OAuth: no Marketplace listing needed; optional Marketplace listing: initial response in 5–10 business days
summary: Public Notion connections use OAuth 2.0, and can be used without a Marketplace listing. The irreversible choice is installation scope: selected workspaces vs any workspace. Marketplace listing, if chosen, has a separate review.
decision: Choose “Any workspace” installation scope if you may list in the Marketplace later. It cannot be changed after creating the connection. A public connection works through OAuth without a Marketplace listing.

branches.name: Internal connection
branches.detail: Useful for one workspace with static token; does not solve end-user cross-workspace connection.

branches.name: Public connection + OAuth
branches.detail: Public OAuth connection with the right installation scope. No Marketplace listing is required for OAuth usage.

branches.name: Marketplace listing
branches.time: Expect an initial response within 5–10 business days (official FAQ)
branches.detail: Optional listing, only for public connections created with Any workspace installation scope; separate review process.

requirements.title: Notion Developer Portal access
requirements.detail: Create a connection; only workspace owners can create internal workspace connections.

requirements.title: Public connection settings
requirements.detail: Configure connection for OAuth, redirect URLs, and permissions in developer portal.

requirements.title: Installation scope is permanent
requirements.detail: Choose Any workspace for broad installation and Marketplace eligibility; Selected workspaces only cannot be changed later.

requirements.title: Page-level user grant
requirements.detail: The user selects which pages are shared. Your integration cannot see pages that were not granted.

requirements.title: Safe access / refresh-token storage
requirements.detail: Exchange authorization code for access and refresh tokens, then rotate/refresh as specified.

steps.title: Decide internal token vs public OAuth
steps.detail: For users from different Notion workspaces, choose the public connection route.

steps.title: Create connection and set capabilities
steps.detail: In the Developer portal choose Public connections → Create new connection; set name, redirect URI, capabilities and installation scope. Choose Any workspace if Marketplace listing may matter.

steps.title: Implement authorization code + refresh flow
steps.detail: Redirect users to Notion, accept code on callback, exchange server-side, encrypt/store access and refresh tokens, support token refresh.

steps.title: Test access to granted and ungranted pages
steps.detail: Have user select pages in consent. Verify permitted reads and expected errors for pages not shared.

steps.title: Optionally apply to Notion Marketplace
steps.detail: Only Any workspace public connections qualify. Create and submit a listing from Marketplace dashboard. The official FAQ says expect initial feedback in 5–10 business days.

blockers.problem: Not found / no access to a page
blockers.solution: Have the user explicitly share the correct Notion page during installation; the connection has no implicit workspace-wide page access.
Ensure redirect URI and client credentials match configuration. Use server-side authorization code exchange.
Read reviewer feedback in the listing dashboard, correct issues with quality, branding or baseline criteria, then resubmit.

blockers.problem: Chose Selected workspaces only but now need Marketplace
blockers.solution: Create a new public connection with Any workspace installation scope; Notion says scope cannot be changed after creation.
